summary: Verify Separation, Replacement, Power Set and Choice using explicit bounding names, and prove the conditional ZFC extension theorem and transitive-model minimality.
abstract: Adjoining a generic filter to a countable transitive model of ZFC gives a set of name values, but proving that this set still satisfies ZFC requires more than closure under pairs and unions. The forcing theorem supplies exact names for definable subsets and set-sized bounds for replacement outputs and internal power sets. Separation then extracts the desired sets, and a named enumeration of possible members yields well-orders in the extension. The result is a countable transitive ZFC-model containing the original model and the filter, with exactly the original ordinals, and contained in every transitive ZF-model containing those data. For Cohen forcing it also contains an explicitly named binary sequence absent from the ground model.
